text: Twiga is a teaching assistant that lives inside WhatsApp. You send it a message. It sends back something you can use in class tomorrow. A lesson plan, an explanation, a set of questions, a marking scheme. It knows the Tanzanian secondary syllabus and the TIE textbooks, and it works in English and in Kiswahili. There is nothing to install and nothing new to learn. If you can send a WhatsApp message, you can use it.

You write in your own words. You do not need commands or any special way of typing. T Twiga im teaching geography form 1 tomorrow, map reading, title is longitudes and latitudes. 40 min period, short plan pls Lesson Title: Longitudes and Latitudes Class: Form 1 • Subject: Geography Time: 40 minutes Lesson Flow: 1. Introduction (8 min) ask which way is north from the door, then draw one horizontal and one vertical line on the board 2. Development (22 min) latitude runs east to west, longitude runs north to south 3. Conclusion (10 min) students give the coordinates of two towns from the board grid It runs on the phone you already have Everything happens in WhatsApp. No app to download, no…

Twiga is useful, and it is not always right. It can name the wrong form level, cite the wrong chapter, or say it saved something it did not save. Read what it sends before you take it to class. This guide shows you where it slips and what to do about it.

How to get a Twiga account. You send one message, a person approves you, then you fill two short forms. All of it happens inside WhatsApp. There is no website and no app to download. You register by sending a message to the Twiga WhatsApp number. The number you send from becomes your account, so there is no username and no password to remember. Do this on your phone Setup uses WhatsApp forms, and forms open in the WhatsApp app. Start on your phone and the whole thing takes a couple of minutes.

Save the Twiga number in your contacts, open the chat and send anything at all. One teacher typed a single greeting and that was the whole sign-up. Hello T Twiga Hello Thank you for registering! Your account is being reviewed by our team. You'll receive a message once approved. Thank you for your patience! You are now registered. Nothing else is asked of you at this point.

A person on the Twiga team reads your request and approves it. This is not automatic, so it is not instant. For the teacher above, the request went at 13:50 and the approval came back at 21:37 the same day. That is close to eight hours. Plan for hours rather than minutes. The approval arrives as a WhatsApp message. Close the chat and carry on with your day. Your phone will tell you when it lands. Messaging again does not move you up the queue A person still has to approve you, and more messages will not reach that person any faster. You also cannot sign up twice, because your phone number is the account. Until setup is finished, anything you send comes back as the same standard reply.

The approval message asks you to reply with one word. It means that word exactly. T Twiga You have been approved 🥳 Congratulations! We approved your request to use Twiga 🦒, your artificially intelligent teaching companion. We support educators teaching the TIE (NECTA) curriculum in Tanzania. To get started, please respond to this message with 'ok'. ok ok Two letters, on their own. A greeting or a question here goes to the normal chat instead, and setup never starts. Send this reply from your phone, because the forms come next.

Twiga sends two forms, one after the other. The first asks for your personal details. The second asks which classes and subjects you teach. There is nothing else to fill in. T Twiga Select the classes you teach 📚 Select the classes you teach from each of the subjects below Please follow the instructions. Tap the form, tick every class and subject you teach, and send it. Twiga uses that list to decide which questions it will answer, so it is worth a careful minute. Do this part in the WhatsApp app The picker is a form, and forms open in the WhatsApp app on your phone. If you started on a laptop, open the same chat on your phone and tap the form there. Nothing is lost and nothing needs…

When the forms are done, Twiga introduces itself and you can start asking. T Twiga Welcome! I'm here to help you with your teaching journey. I'm Twiga 🦒, your teaching assistant. I can help you with questions related to the classes you teach, search the content, and generate exercises you can use in your classes. To update your personal or subject information, type 'settings' in the chat. Let's get started! Just talk to me like a colleague. That last line is the best advice on this page. You do not need special wording. Type the way you would text a colleague in the staff room.

Both forms stay open to you. Send the bare word settings in the chat at any time. Two buttons come back, one for your personal details and one for your classes and subjects. settings Teachers change subjects between terms, so you will use this again. The subjects form has one trap worth knowing about before you open it, and the next page covers it.

What you see What to do Nothing at all after your first message Check you sent it to the right number. If the chat shows the review notice, you are registered and waiting. Approval can take hours. The form bubble says it cannot be displayed Open the chat on the WhatsApp phone app and tap it again. You replied with something other than ok Send ok on its own. Nothing is broken. You finished setup but Twiga refuses your subject Your profile is probably wrong. Send settings and fix the class list. Twiga only answers for the subjects and forms saved on your profile. Here is how to set that list, and how to prove it saved. Your profile holds the classes you teach. Twiga checks it before every answer. Ask about a subject that is not on the list and it will refuse, politely, and tell you what it does have for you. T Twiga Do you have teaching materials for primary schools? I currently support only secondary school teachers, specifically for Form 1 and Form 2 subjects in the Tanzanian National Curriculum. Unfortunately, I do not have materials for primary school levels at this time. That is why a wrong profile feels like a broken Twiga. The content may be there. Twiga just does not think…

Send one word. Not a slash, not a sentence, just the word on its own. settings T Twiga settings Welcome to the Settings Menu, please select what you want to update. This is an automatic message 🦒 [ Personal Info ] [ Classes and Subjects ] Classes and Subjects Two buttons come back. Personal Info is your name and school. Classes and Subjects is the one that decides which questions get answered. Tap the second one and a form opens. Send settings from your phone The form opens in the WhatsApp app, so send settings from your phone rather than from a laptop. The picker then opens where you can tap it.

This is the part that catches people. The form does not add to your profile. It replaces it. Whatever you tick becomes the whole list, and anything you leave unticked is dropped, even if it was saved last term. One teacher had three subjects saved across Form 1 and Form 2. He opened the form, ticked Geography for Forms 1 to 4, and sent it. Afterwards his profile held Geography and nothing else. The other three subjects were gone. Do it in one pass Before you send the form, look down the whole list. Tick every subject and every form level you teach this term, including the ones that were already there.

When you send the form, Twiga replies with nothing at all. No confirmation, no summary, no error. This is a known fault. Silence here does not mean the save failed. Do not sit waiting for a reply and do not fill the form again. Check it instead.

Asking is the only feedback there is. Type the question in your own words and read the answer against your timetable. what subjects am i teaching? T Twiga what subjects am i teaching? You are teaching Geography 🌎 for Form 1, Form 2, Form 3, and Form 4. Let me know if you'd like support with lesson content, practice questions, or teaching tips for any of these classes! Read the subjects and read the form levels. Anything missing from that sentence is something Twiga will refuse to help you with tomorrow.

Send settings again There is no limit on how many times you can change it. Tap Classes and Subjects On your phone, so the form opens. Tick the full list, not the missing part Remember that it replaces. Ticking only the subject you forgot will wipe the ones that were already right. Ask what you teach Then read it back. Repeat until the sentence matches your timetable. Which subjects can you pick? The form itself is the only reliable answer, and what it offers has changed over time. Do not plan around a list you read somewhere else. Open the form and look, then confirm with the question above.

Personal Info opens a different form, for your name and school details. It has one oddity of its own: Twiga may greet you by a name you never typed. Fixing Your Profile Change your name and school details, and confirm the change was saved. Quick Start Your profile is set. Now send a request you can use in class today.

One real conversation, start to finish. A teacher with twelve minutes before class gets what he needs in one message, then gets the next thing without starting over. Do not test Twiga with a made-up question. Ask it for the lesson you are actually teaching next. The answers get sharper the more real the request is, and you end up with something you can carry into the room.

Here is a real one. A teacher had a Form 1 maths class starting in twelve minutes and could not remember what came after integers. T Twiga Mambo! I have my Form 1 maths class in 12 minutes and I just realised I forgot what topic comes after integers. Help!! Mambo! No worries, I've got you covered. 😊 After Integers, the next topic in Form 1 Mathematics is Fractions. This includes: - Meaning and types of fractions (proper, improper, mixed) - Converting between improper fractions and mixed numbers - Operations on fractions (add, subtract, multiply, divide) - Solving problems involving fractions Let me know if you'd like: - A quick 2-minute summary for students? - One practice question to…

headingText: The shape you get by default
text: That answer is long. It gives the topic, four subtopics, and three offers of what to do next. That is Twiga's default shape when you do not say what you want back. It is a good answer in a free period. With twelve minutes it is more than you can read. So say the shape you want, in the message itself.

Three minutes later the same teacher moved on to a different class, a different subject and a different form level. He said so in the same chat, and he said exactly how much he wanted. T Twiga ok recap im now going to physics form 2. give me a 1-line intro for newtons first law that 14 year olds will actually remember "An object will stay still or keep moving in a straight line unless a force, like a push, pull, or stop, makes it change!" One line asked for, one line back. The words that did the work were 1-line and that 14 year olds will actually remember . Small words like those change the whole answer.

headingText: Keep going in the same chat
text: You never have to start again. The chat remembers what you have been talking about, so the next request can lean on the last one. Five minutes from an emergency staff meeting, the same teacher sent this: T Twiga can you set me a quick 3 question exit ticket for the law you just gave me? mixed difficulty Of course! Here's a quick 3-question exit ticket on Newton's First Law, easy, medium, and challenge: 1. What happens to a ball lying on the ground if no one kicks it? Explain using Newton's First Law. 2. A passenger in a moving car jerks forward when the car suddenly stops. Use Newton's First Law to explain why. 3. True or False: An object in motion always needs a force to keep moving.…

headingText: Read it before you teach it
text: Twiga's content comes from the TIE textbooks. Even so, a topic order, an intro line and an exit ticket are all worth one look against your own scheme of work. You are not proofreading a document. You are checking that it says what you expected. That is thirty seconds, and you have twelve minutes.

headingText: If your subject is not covered
text: Twiga does not cover everything. In this same session the teacher asked about English Literature and was told no. It answers for secondary school only, and only for the subjects and forms on your profile. So make your first real request one it can answer. If you are not sure what is on your profile, ask it. what subjects am i teaching?

Pick your next lesson and send one message that names the subject, the form, the topic and what you want back. For example: I have my Form 1 maths class in 15 minutes. What topic comes after integers? How to Ask Twiga The five things to put in a message so the first answer is the one you wanted. Checking Twiga's Answers The one minute check that catches a wrong form level or a source from another subject.

Five things go in one message. Put them all in and the first answer is usable, so you do not spend a turn being asked for them. A vague request costs you a message. Twiga writes back asking for the details it needed, you send them, and only then do you get your answer. Between lessons that is a minute you did not have. T Twiga i would like to have a practice activity Happy to help with a practice activity! 📑 To make one you can actually use, just tell me: - Subject - Form (e.g. Form 1 or 2) - Topic (e.g. map reading, forces) - What you want (questions, activity, lesson tips) And I'll send it right away! That list is Twiga's own. It asks for the same four things every time. So send them…

Put in Looks like Subject geography, book keeping, physics Form form 1, form 2 Topic map reading, longitudes and latitudes, trial balance. For a lesson plan, give the lesson title too. What you want, and how many a practice activity, 5 questions, a 1-line intro, mixed difficulty Anything about your class i have no materials, only 30 minutes, they are weak on fractions The fifth one is the one teachers leave out, and it is the one that changes the answer most. Twiga never asks for it.

You do not need neat sentences. This is one lowercase line typed on a phone, and it answers every item on the list. geography form 1, map reading, longitudes and latitudes. i need a practice activity, 5 questions mixed difficulty. i have no materials to show them physically T Twiga geography form 1, map reading, longitudes and latitudes. i need a practice activity, 5 questions mixed difficulty. i have no materials to show them physically Practice Activity: Longitudes and Latitudes Geography, Form 1, no materials needed 1. In your own words, what is a line of latitude? 2. Which line divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres? 3. Use your arms to show the class the direction…

Say how much and in what form, and you get that. Leave it out and you get Twiga's long default answer with a menu of offers at the end. All of these are real and all of them worked: 5 questions and 3 question set the count. mixed difficulty gets you an easy one, a medium one and a hard one. 1-line gets you one line, not a paragraph. without sounding like a robot changes the language it uses. short lesson plan keeps a plan down to one period.

Send one thing, wait for the answer, then send the next. This sounds fussy. It is not. One teacher sent a request about the two-column cash book. Twenty-one seconds later, before any answer came, he sent a second unrelated question. Both were lost. The only replies were two error messages. Do not stack messages If you have two things to ask, ask the first, read the answer, then ask the second. Twiga follows the thread, so the second one can be short.

Most replies end with two or three offers. "Want the marking guide or a printable version?" Do not answer those with a bare yes . Twiga cannot tell which one you meant, so it asks, and you have lost a turn. Name the thing instead. yes give me the printable version Short follow-ups are fine once the chat has context. This one carries a count, a format, a difficulty and the topic, in one line, without naming the topic at all: T Twiga can you set me a quick 3 question exit ticket on this? mixed difficulty Of course! A 3-question exit ticket on Longitudes and Latitudes, easy, medium, challenge: 1. Latitude lines run in which direction, east to west or north to south? 2. Name the 0° line of…

headingText: Write in the language you teach in
text: Twiga reads English and Kiswahili. Ask in Kiswahili and it answers in Kiswahili. One teacher asked for a Book Keeping lesson plan on the trial balance in Kiswahili, and the whole plan came back in Kiswahili. The five ingredients are the same in either language, so pick the one you are quicker in.

A usable answer is not a checked answer. Before any of this goes to a class, read the numbers and read the form level. Then look at the bottom of the reply, where it says which book the content came from. Checking Twiga's Answers The one minute check on any reply before it goes into a classroom. Requesting a Lesson Plan What a lesson plan request needs on top of these five, including the lesson title.

A one minute check on any answer before it goes into a classroom. It is mostly right, and the check catches the times it is confidently wrong. Twiga writes well. Every answer arrives tidy, structured and ready to use, whether it is correct or not. So a bad answer does not look bad. It looks exactly like a good one. The one thing that gives it away is at the bottom. Some answers end with a Sources: block naming the TIE books behind each claim. Read that block and you catch most of the trouble.

Scroll to the bottom Look for a Sources: list. Not every answer has one. Read the subject in each line It should be your subject. Not a related one, not another one. Read the form Form One, Form Two, Form Three, Form Four. It should be the form you asked for. Match the numbers to the claims Find where the little bracketed numbers sit in the answer, and see whether that source could really be about that sentence. If any of those fail, keep the answer as your own background reading. Just do not hand it to a class as textbook material.

text: A teacher asked for a Book Keeping lesson plan on the trial balance. The plan that came back was good. Its one source was not. New content (15 min) - A Trial Balance lists the closing balances of every ledger account, debit on the left and credit on the right - The debit total must equal the credit total, and if it is not equal there is an error [1] Sources: - [1] Geography for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form Two, Chapter Two (Agriculture) hold on. [1] is a geography agriculture chapter. thats not my subject The accounting rule itself is correct. The source…

headingText: A source from the wrong form
text: This one is harder to catch. The answer names the wrong form out loud, in its first line, and the eye still slides past it. T Twiga and for my geography class, form 1 map reading, types of maps Based on the official TIE Geography textbook for Form 3, the two main types of maps are: Topographical Maps These show both natural (physical) and man-made features of an area [1] Statistical Maps These give quantitative information about the distribution of a phenomenon [4] Sources: - [1] Geography for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form Three, Elementary Surveying - [4] Geography for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form Three, Elementary Surveying form three, every line. i asked form 1. keeping…

Most answers have none. In five months of one teacher's real use, only four answers out of roughly thirty carried a Sources: block. So a missing block is not a warning sign. It just means you are reading general knowledge that happens to be about your topic. Useful, often right, and worth a look in the book before you teach it as what the textbook says. And a block that is there is not a guarantee either. Read it.

headingText: Look at the chapter names too
text: Sources can be sloppy inside a single answer. In one Form 1 Mathematics reply, all five sources misspelled the book as Methematics for Secondary Schools . In the same list, a chapter called Coordinate Geometry was cited twice. Once for rounding off decimals, and once for the perimeter and area of basic shapes. You do not have to study the block. Just ask yourself whether that chapter could really hold the fact it is being used to prove.

headingText: What a good block looks like
text: Good ones exist, and they are what you are comparing against. One Book Keeping answer covering Form 1 and Form 2 topics cited Book-Keeping for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form One and Form Two . The chapter names matched the topics they sat under. Right subject, right forms, sensible chapters.

Demote it, do not delete it. A Form 3 answer to a Form 1 question is still good reading for you. It is just not class material. Ask again, with the form level first. Start the message with the form you teach, then the subject and the topic. Check the rule in the book. If a claim carries a source from another subject, open your own textbook for that one line before you teach it. Check your profile. If answers keep coming back for the wrong form, your saved class list may be wrong. It is a habit, not a warning Twiga is useful and mostly right. This check costs a minute and it catches the small number of times it is confidently wrong. Do it the same way every time and you stop thinking about…

headingText: Do I need to install anything?
text: No. Everything happens in a WhatsApp chat, in the app you already have. There is nothing to download and no website to sign in to. T Twiga hi. before i tell the other teachers about this, do i need to download anything? I'm Twiga, your teaching assistant bot developed by the Tanzania AI Community. Everything happens right here in this chat, there's nothing to install. I can: - Explain concepts from the official TIE textbooks - Create NECTA-style practice questions - Provide teaching tips and lesson ideas Just tell me the subject and topic. One exception. The setup forms only open in the WhatsApp phone app, not in WhatsApp Web or Desktop. Everything after setup works anywhere.

There is no fee and no subscription. In five months of one teacher's real use there was never a payment prompt or a trial that ran out. What you spend is WhatsApp data, at your normal rate. Almost everything both ways is text, so it is small. The only heavy items are PDF files, such as a mock exam and its marking scheme. Those download only when you tap them.
Your phone number is your account. There is no email address, no username and no password. You register by sending one message, and then a person on the Twiga team approves you.

headingText: Can I send a voice note or a photo?
text: No. Twiga reads text only. Anything else comes back the same way. T Twiga [8 second voice note] Sorry, I only understand textual messages. Do not type your question as a photo caption One teacher sent a photo with his question typed in the caption. The photo was refused and the caption went with it. Twiga never saw the question. Type your question as a message of its own. Media you send can also sit unread in the chat and get refused much later. If a "textual messages" reply turns up out of nowhere, it is probably answering an old photo or voice note, not what you just typed.

Yes. Twiga reads English and Kiswahili. Ask in Kiswahili and the answer comes back in Kiswahili. One teacher asked for a Book Keeping lesson plan on the trial balance in Kiswahili and got the whole plan in Kiswahili. Write in whichever language you are quicker in.

headingText: Does it remember what I asked before?
text: Inside a conversation, yes. Ask what your last question was and it tells you, along with the one before it. That is what lets you say "the law you just gave me" instead of typing it all again. It is not a record of your term. Asked for the very first question ever sent to it, it failed twice with an error. Treat the chat as a conversation, not an archive. Keep what you want to reuse Star the message in WhatsApp, or save the PDF to your phone. A lesson plan or an exam paper you want again next term should be saved by you, not looked up later by asking.

headingText: Does it know my name and my school?
text: It knows what is in your profile, and that is what you typed into the setup forms. Ask it directly and it will tell you it does not hold your personal details, then point you at settings . In practice it may still greet you by a name. One teacher was called "Teacher Edgar" and "Mr. Edgar" in a chat where his WhatsApp name was something else entirely. If it uses a name that is not yours, send settings , open Personal Info and correct it.

headingText: Which subjects and forms does it cover?
text: Secondary school only. Asked directly, it says it covers Book Keeping, Mathematics and Physics for Form 1 and Form 2. It has refused a request for primary school materials, and another for English Literature. In practice it has also answered Geography requests in full, including lesson plans and a whole mock exam. So what it says it covers and what it will actually answer do not fully agree. The list on your own profile is what governs your chat.
Yes, and it never sounds wrong. The most common problem is an answer drawn from a different form level than the one you asked for. Checking Twiga's Answers is the one minute check that catches it.

Some jobs really are slow. A full mock exam takes about ten minutes and Twiga tells you so while it works. A reply that never arrives is a different thing, and When Twiga Doesn't Reply covers how to tell them apart.

text: One. settings , sent on its own, opens your profile. Every other thing you send is plain language. settings

Write to dev@ai.or.tz . That address only ever appears inside an error message, so copy it down now rather than waiting to be shown it. Include three things so they can find what went wrong: The date and time it happened. The exact message you sent. The phone number you use with Twiga. One message with five details gets a plan you can teach as it is. Here is what to put in that message, and what you get back when you leave something out. It is evening. You teach the lesson tomorrow morning, and you do not want to answer three questions from a bot before you see anything. You do not have to. Twiga can build the whole plan from your first message, as long as that message carries five details.

headingText: Class context is the detail with teeth
text: One teacher asked for the same Geography lesson without saying what he had. The plan came back with a Materials Needed list: a globe or world map with grid lines, a map of Tanzania with grid lines, coloured pencils, flashcards, a chalkboard or projector, and a protractor. Nothing in that plan is wrong. It just could not be taught in his room. He had no physical materials at all. When he said so, Twiga answered in seconds with low resource ideas. Use your body as a globe. Stand in front of the class as the Earth's axis. Same topic, same bot, one extra line in the request. The line to add i have no teaching aids at all, just a chalkboard Or say what you do have. A textbook and one wall map is…

headingText: What a short request gets you
text: Here is the same job done in five words. T Twiga nitengenezee kwa ajili ya biolojia Lesson Plan: Biolojia (Fomu 1) Wakati: Somo la 40 Dakika Mada: Ukuaji (Growth) No form, no topic, no length. Twiga chose all three on its own: Form 1, the topic Ukuaji, a 40 minute period. It did not ask first, and it did not say it was guessing. This is the trap. The plan looks finished. It is just not the lesson you are teaching.

headingText: Check it before you teach it
text: A full plan can come back in seconds. The most complete request in our chat logs named the subject, the form, the topic and the language in one line. The plan came back 21 seconds later. Fast is not the same as correct. Two things to read before class. The class and topic in the header. If Twiga guessed a form or a topic you did not name, it will be sitting right at the top. The sources footer. One Form 2 Book Keeping plan on trial balance ended with a source line pointing at a Geography book, Form Two, Chapter Two, on Agriculture. That is the wrong book altogether.

Sometimes Twiga sends Creating a lesson plan, please hold... and then sends nothing at all. This is a real fault. One teacher waited eight minutes and asked again. Twiga replied that it had already sent the full plan above. It had not. Do not keep waiting. Do one of these two things. Send can i get the printable version . That is what the teacher did, and the missing plan arrived. Send your original one line request again, word for word.

Twiga works in Kiswahili and in English. The five details are the same in either language. Add kiswahili tafadhali if you want the plan itself in Kiswahili. That 21 second plan was asked for in Kiswahili. The teacher wrote in Kiswahili, asked for a Kiswahili plan, and got one.

pageTitle: What's in a Twiga Lesson Plan
text: One thing never broke. In all three plans the stage minutes add to the stated duration. 10 plus 15 plus 15 plus 5 is the 45 minutes above. The other two plans add to 40. But Twiga chose those durations itself. It picked 40, 40 and 45 without being asked. Its own questions never ask how long your period is. If you teach an 80 minute period or a double, say so when you ask. See Requesting a Lesson Plan for the rest of what belongs in that first message.

Competences appeared in none of the plans it actually sent. Do not assume any section will be there because Twiga said so. If your form needs a row, ask for that row by name.

Arusha, Tanzania ________ 2. London, United Kingdom ________ 3. Sydney, Australia ________ B. Short answer 4. Why does latitude affect climate? 5. Why does longitude affect time? Copy this into Word or Google Docs to print. I can't send files on WhatsApp directly. Quizzes and group activities work the same way. Ask in the same chat. Printable does not mean a file Twiga cannot send a PDF or any other attachment on WhatsApp.…

pageTitle: What's in a Twiga Lesson Plan
headingText: Before you copy it into your plan book
text: Read the section headings first. Note anything your plan book needs that is not there. Ask for each missing section by name, in the same chat. Check the duration matches your period, and check the stage minutes against it. Read the content itself, not just the shape. A plan can be laid out perfectly and still cite the wrong book.

Ask Twiga what topic comes next, get the topic and subtopic list for your form, and check it against your printed syllabus before it goes in your scheme of work. You are ten minutes from class and you cannot remember what topic comes after the one you just finished. Or you are writing a scheme of work and you want the whole form in front of you. Twiga answers both from the TIE curriculum, on your phone, in under a minute. It is fastest at the small question. Ask where you are in the sequence, not for the whole syllabus.

Name three things: the subject, the form, and the topic you have just finished. That is the whole message. T Twiga Mambo! I have my Form 1 maths class in 12 minutes and I just realised I forgot what topic comes after integers. Help!! Mambo! No worries, I've got you covered. 😊 After Integers, the next topic in Form 1 Mathematics is Fractions. This includes: - Meaning and types of fractions (proper, improper, mixed) - Converting between improper fractions and mixed numbers - Operations on fractions (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) - Solving problems involving fractions Let me know if you'd like a quick 2-minute summary for students, or one practice question to start the…

When you have time to sit down, ask for the full list. Say why you want it. Telling Twiga you are writing a scheme of work gets you the whole form instead of one topic. T Twiga asante. and the full topic list for form 1 maths? im writing my scheme of work Based on the official Tanzanian Institute of Education (TIE) curriculum for Mathematics Form 1, the main topics covered are: 1. Numbers and Operations: whole numbers, integers, fractions, decimals; BODMAS [1] 2. Factors and Multiples: prime factors, GCF, LCM 3. Fractions and Decimals: conversion, operations, rounding off [2] 4. Ratios, Proportions and Percentages [3] 5. Algebra: expressions, substitution, simple linear equations [4] 6.…

headingText: Open one topic at a time
text: Once a topic list is on the screen, you do not have to repeat yourself. Name the topic and ask for its subtopics. T Twiga what are the subtopics for statistics The subtopics for Statistics in Form 1 Mathematics are: - Data collection and presentation (tables, bar graphs, pie charts) - Measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) Would you like a brief explanation of any of these from the textbook, or practice questions for your students? Right after a reply about one topic, even what are the subtopics for it is enough. Take the topics one at a time. Asking for every subtopic in the whole form at once gives you a wall of text you will not read on a phone.

Two forms in one message. Do you carry the same subject across two classes? Ask for both together. You get one reply with both lists in it, one after the other, and a Sources block naming both books. we are going to explore book keeping form 1&2. can you tell me what topics are covered for those 2 classes Which topic to start with. Twiga will also answer planning questions about the order you teach in. what topic in form one is the easiest to teach? The reply names one topic from the subject on your profile. Better, it gives the reasons: students need no prior knowledge for it, it is close to everyday life, and it is easy to run activities around. Treat that as a colleague's opinion, not as…

headingText: Check the list before you use it
text: Twiga is a good way to find your place in the sequence. It is not the authority on what the sequence is. Your printed syllabus is. Topic counts are not reliable Asked how many topics Mathematics Form 1 has, Twiga answered six in March and ten in May. The two lists do not line up with each other. In another chat it said Biology Form 1 has seven topics. Less than a minute later it said three of those seven are really Form 2 content. Nothing new had been said in between. So never copy a Twiga topic count into a document as fact. If the count matters, ask again in a fresh message and compare the two answers. Then settle it with the book. Before a list goes into your scheme of work: Tick every…

Never ask Twiga about terms or dates Every calendar answer in the chat log came back wrong. Twiga has said Term 1 runs August to October. It put Term 2 at November to March of the next year, with April as a holiday carrying the end of year exams. The Tanzanian academic year runs January to December. It also said there are three terms, then two terms, less than a minute apart. Term dates, exam weeks and the school calendar come from your head of department and the school notice board. Use Twiga for the content of the syllabus, not for when you teach it.

headingText: When you get the wrong subject
text: Twiga answers against the subjects and forms saved on your profile. If you ask about Mathematics and get Geography back, that is your profile talking, not a broken answer. Fix the profile and ask again. See Choosing Your Subjects . If the reply is vague or gives you the wrong form, add the missing details and send it again. Subject, form and topic in one message get you further than three short messages do.

Ask Twiga to explain one concept from the TIE textbook, so you can check your own understanding the night before you teach it. Then read the Sources block to see which book, and which form, the answer came from. You are teaching a topic tomorrow. You know it, mostly. You would still like to see it written down the way the textbook writes it, before you stand in front of thirty students. That is what this page is for. It is about what the content is , not how to deliver it. Do you want the words to say in class, the activity, the board work? Ask for that instead, and see Ask How to Teach It, Not What It Is .

One line. The word explain , the topic, the form, the subject. explain types of maps for form 3 geography Twiga suggests this one itself. Asked how a teacher should use it, it put this first on the list. Here is the pattern in its own words: Need to clarify a concept before teaching? Just say: “Explain double entry system for Form 1 Book Keeping”. I'll give you a textbook-accurate explanation using content from the official TIE syllabus, so you're always aligned with what students need to know. Saying why you are asking helps too. “im teaching it tomorrow and i want to check what i know is right first” tells Twiga you want the content, not a lesson.

headingText: When it says it cannot find the topic
text: Sometimes the first ask returns nothing. Twiga says so plainly instead of making something up. That message is honest, and it is where the fix starts. T Twiga explain map reading for form 1 geography. im teaching it tomorrow and i want to check what i know is right first I could not find this information in the textbook content for your class. If you want, I can help with a related topic that is covered. yes, which subtopics under map reading are covered? Could you please clarify which specific topic or subtopic under Map Reading you'd like materials for? For example: - Types of maps - Map scales - Grid references - Compass directions - Features on topographic maps Let me know so I can…

A narrowed ask gets a real answer. Look at what arrives with it. There are little numbers inside the text, and a Sources list at the bottom naming the book and the chapter. T Twiga Based on the official TIE Geography textbook for Form 3, the two main types of maps are: - Topographical Maps These show both natural (physical) and man-made (cultural) features of an area [1]. Natural features include mountains, valleys, rivers, lakes and forests [2]. - Statistical Maps These give quantitative information about the distribution of a phenomenon [4]. They are also called distribution maps, and dot maps are a common example [5]. Would you like me to create a practice exercise or a lesson plan on…

headingText: Check the form it came from
text: This is the trap on this page, and it is easy to miss. The teacher above asked about Form 1 . The answer opens “for Form 3”, and every source line reads “Student's Book Form Three”. Twiga never flagged the change of level. The closing offer says “for Form 3?”, and that is the only other hint you get. So the check is one question: Does the Sources line name the book for the form I teach? A Form 3 explanation is not wrong. It is just above your Form 1 class, and it can carry content the syllabus does not ask of them. If you teach it as it stands, you teach too much. When the form does not match, do this: Ask again and name the form in the message itself. For example: explain types of maps…

headingText: What a citation does not prove
text: The Sources block is a pointer, not proof. The book and chapter names are real, but they are rough: In the Types of Maps answer, every number points at the same chapter, “Elementary Surveying”. In a Mathematics answer, two unrelated topics both point at a chapter called “Coordinate Geometry”. The book title is misspelled “Methematics” in every line of that block. So a Sources block tells you two things and no more: the answer came from a textbook, and which form's book it was. It does not give you a page number. It is not a promise that the sentence above it is correct. Open the book.

pageTitle: Ask How to Teach It, Not What It Is
text: One topic can give you two very different answers. Ask what the topic is and you get the syllabus. Ask how to teach it and you get sentences you can say to the class. You already know the topic. It is on the scheme of work and you are teaching it in the morning. What you do not have is the first thing to say when you are standing in front of forty students. That is a different question, and Twiga answers it only if you ask it. Send the topic name and you get the curriculum. Ask how to teach it and you get words you can say.

pageTitle: Ask How to Teach It, Not What It Is
headingText: The same topic, asked two ways
text: Here is one teacher, one topic, two minutes apart. Watch what changes in the reply when the question changes.
